A claim to a dead resource is the only claim the plains can still honour, and this pack inherits that estate by eating it: worked-out ground, dead miners and standing spoil are the same gradient, so scavenging and holding the worked-out face are the same act.

The one public account on the plains is a weight of spoil moved by every crew, kept where the crews can read it, and a scavenger's entire range is a function of where crews break and where they leave something; the tally is therefore the pack's map and the pack's reason to stay out of the guilds' way.

A breakthrough calendar is a schedule published a season ahead, and knowing it would let a pack predict where bodies will be produced rather than only where they were; no guild has ever taught it to a scavenger and every guild has had the same reason.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said and the village remembers them otherwise, and the Cinder Famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present; a pack eats the difference, which is why the disagreement is a food supply and a grievance at the same time.

No march order on the plains can be enforced by measurement, so every claim is settled by a marker left standing, and a scavenger is the population that makes standing a question rather than a formality: nothing survives a gradient that feeds on it.

Spoil does not disperse where spatial law is unspent, so forty years of it stands on the last unworked iron, and the waste guild that moves it reads the same heap as a cost and a pack reads it as a larder that has been standing still for four decades.

The guild that moves the heap off the seam floor cannot employ what it cannot catch, so the packs are tolerated inside its charter rather than members of it, and the arrangement is the reason the guild's tally is public where the extraction guild's is not.

A pack has no roll of its own, so the mortuary college's reading of a death is the only count that exists, and a scavenger that is entered as a cause of death and never as a population is how a species with no census ends up owning the census.

The culture publishes the whole recovery and forbids displaying the fragments again, and the prohibition is the only thing that keeps the debris unclaimed: nobody may cite a fragment nobody has seen, so the pack has an exclusive range the register household does not know it has.

The commons of the mortal plains works because nobody here expects to ascend and the work is judged by what survives the season, and that is precisely the rule a pack is shaped by: take what is left, be where the season is ending, and do not stay.

The town at the foot of the stair is the only settlement on the tier whose whole population is visitors, and the packs hold the gradient immediately below it where arrivals stop being people and become weight.

The plains' one large migratory herd returns on a cycle nobody on the ground has predicted and is therefore the tier's only moving calendar, so the pack's timing is borrowed wholesale from an animal it does not hunt and cannot follow without eating it.

A whole profession exists because spatial law is unspent, carrying waste that cannot be made to disperse, and haulage is what converts a standing heap into a trail of dropped weight; remove the profession and the pack has a larder nobody ever opens.

A scavenger is born where the dead are the most reliable food, and it is the exhaustion of one seam that put four decades of worked-out ground, dead crews and unmoved spoil onto a single leeward gradient for the first time.

Strata under the plains carry tool marks that imply a hand on a frame that seats three law groups and none of them moves distance, and the only population that reaches the bottom of an unmoved spoil heap without moving anything is the one that cannot carry anything at all.

The Sealed Core holds that the dead are unsealed at burial and their core resumes work in the frame, so on the plains a body is fuel and the dead are fuel not yet spent; a pack eats the unspent remainder and is the only population that would agree with the theology.

The afterlife the same faith teaches is a court of resumed fuel, and a pack's actual experience is that everything a court counts as resumed is instead carried off a slope inside a season, which is the gap that makes the faith need a prohibition against discussing scavengers.

In a mortal world nothing carries an element because elemental law was never written: seasons drift unanchored and ore has no affinity. The pack's fire affinity is therefore an appetite rather than a nature, which is why it eats the dead instead of becoming one of them.

The households that were working the seam hold the worked-out face as a title, and the species that breathes the belt's airborne grit is not a tenant of that title so much as its standing crop, turning up wherever a face is being cut.

The heap clan holds a crew and a number on a public spoil tally and no land at all, and the herd that walks the belt without folding it into an ore bed has the same relationship to the face: continuous presence, no claim, and a total dependence on somebody else's shift calendar.

Both are the belt's fire-adjacent answer to living on hot stone: the quenchbound house signs every child to a furnace because a fire-affinity body with no seated elemental law must burn its own reserve, and the ashwalker avoids that expense by filtering the grit instead of refining it.

Nobody on the plains expects to ascend and the work is judged by what survives the season, and this is the belt's commons: the one population whose survival is measured in kilograms of air rather than in harvests, and whose presence on the ground is itself the cost of cutting the face.

A league of the two coasts formed the moment the sea became worth owning, which is the first tier where a coastline holds its shape, and the league's entire commercial premise requires a member who can serve both shores without a change of body.

The Immortal Court's second layer is the one ground where a law is written twice and the second writing wins, and a keyed masonry body is what holds ground whose composition is unsettled, because it cannot be relocated and therefore cannot be re-keyed to a different list.

Every member came from a lineage that stopped one gate short of the ceiling with no cultivator left to produce, and this is the population that stops one gate short with no cultivator to produce by design; the two are the same arithmetic arriving from opposite directions.

A trial ground on a frame that cannot say where anything is is laid out as a ring of standing markers spaced by ear, and possession on the plains is proven by a marker standing, so this species is not merely the markers, it is the only marker that cannot be moved by the party disputing the claim.

The published explanation covers why the densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of their tier, and it was written by people with a commercial interest in that hole staying a hole; this body's actual wall is the fourth gate and no naming reaches it.

The densest bodies stop one gate short of the end of their own tier and whoever benefits from an unexplained ceiling wants the hole shut, while the single densest body in the record stops at the fourth gate for a reason that has been fully understood since it was first cast and is still not in the assay.

The cleft's moss maps the jade gradient and dies back over any cut ground, so cutting the jade also grazes the only map of where the seam runs, and the holdfast answers the loss of the map by keying bodies into the workings, which is the industry that keeps destroying it.

Every holder of that shore built their wall facing arrivals because a rift closes when the out-of-range law value returns inside its range, and a masonry body cannot be turned around once keyed, so the wall's orientation is a decision its owner can never revisit.

Ore is the one thing on the plains a core can be caged in, and the work at the face needs a body that carries and does not fatigue, so the guild's charter is also the setting's first written labour arrangement for a population that cannot be dismissed.

The lodge does not sell houses or passages but bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, and this is the limiting case of the product: a body that exists on exactly one frame and cannot be carried to another at any price.

A guild of builders held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain in bodies never designed to take the meridian burn, and this is the accident the practice was invented to survive: a body where hardening finished before the practice began.

The guild builds and then guards what it builds and takes as its measure that it is tested from the other side, so the only population that is permanently on the tested side is the one whose members were installed rather than invited.

A garrison holding ground its own faction cannot staff from, where every soul inside the walls is a visitor, is a fort whose wall can be staffed by a body that cannot be dismissed and cannot be posted: the wall is the garrison and the garrison is the reason the wall is not manned.

Jade runs as a gradient rather than a pocket so the cutters live in falling series of thin hard workings, and each working is a cut too small to be shored by anything that might leave, which is the entire architectural requirement this species was built for.

The lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it and is the only reliable marker that a trial has been held, and this body carries it on its own interior, which is why it is the one cultivator in the record nobody has ever had to search for.

Iron ore is the mortal tier's only dense material and the only thing here a body can be caged in, and a masonry body is ore that achieved the same density metabolically, so the exhaustion of the seam is the end of the setting's densest body as well as its first bottleneck.

Jade holds qi and will not grow a crop, so whoever provisions the cutters owns the cleft more durably than whoever digs it, and a body that eats nothing and must be installed by hand is provisioned by the same clause that feeds everybody else on the site.

Realms three and four turned out to be a metallurgy problem before they were a spiritual one, and this is the population the problem created: a load-bearing body cast in the one material the tier could afford, in an era that thought it was building gates.

The densest bodies stop one gate short of the end of their own tier and the era that produced the stop has no spare seat to stand outside on, and a one-cavity interior with a tidal mineral circulation is the structure that consequence built and then could not explain.

The era that produced the stop is the one era with no spare seat to stand outside on, and a masonry body's single tidal cavity is exactly such a place: no second chamber to hold a law apart from its effect and observe it, so the one body in the setting designed to answer the question was designed to prevent it.

The class of mortal-tier offices that by construction can only be filled by non-residents is the reason a polity on the lowest tier is a caretaker government, and a body installed into a wall is the extreme non-resident: present, load-bearing, and accountable to nobody who can send it anywhere.

Physical law governs material hardness and energy density, and this is the mortal tier's answer to it taken far enough that the answer became a species: hardness is what made the frame durable and what removed the organ pairs the fifth gate demands.

A line holding an asset that cannot be sold, cannot be proven and pays upkeep on nothing, and a species that can certify a death but has never once been able to certify an absence is the only population that could settle such a claim and never has.
